name: Black hole
hook: The collapsed star whose gravity traps light — and the man who made it famous.

facts.label: gravity
facts.statement: A black hole's gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape it.

facts.label: the event horizon
facts.statement: The event horizon is the boundary of a black hole, the point beyond which escape would require exceeding the speed of light.

facts.label: the singularity
facts.statement: At the center of a black hole, matter collapses to a singularity — a point of zero volume and infinite density.

facts.label: Stephen Hawking
facts.statement: Stephen Hawking calculated in 1974 that black holes emit radiation and are not completely black; his bestseller A Brief History of Time is subtitled From the Big Bang to Black Holes.

facts.label: Cygnus X-1
facts.statement: Cygnus X-1, in the constellation Cygnus the Swan, was the first black hole identified.

facts.label: Sagittarius A*
facts.statement: Sagittarius A*, at the center of the Milky Way, is a supermassive black hole about 4.3 million times the mass of the Sun.

facts.label: the name
facts.statement: John Michell proposed the idea in 1783, and physicist John Wheeler coined the term black hole as shorthand for completely collapsed objects.
